physical.weight-note: 98 lb (44.45 kg) with power supplies and fans installed, 76 lb (34.47 kg) chassis only (guide Table 32)

power.power-input-ac: 100 to 240 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz; 19.36 A at 100 to 127 VAC, 10.95 A at 200 to 240 VAC (guide Table 19)

ac-f2b.description: QFX5220-128C-AFO: four 1600 W AC supplies (JPSU-1600W-AC-AFO) and six front-to-back fan modules (QFX5220-128C-FANAO). All have a Juniper gold handle and the label AIR OUT (guide Tables 3, 16 and 18).

chas.description: QFX5220-128C-CHAS, the spare chassis, shipped without power supplies or fan modules. Either AC or DC supplies are ordered separately, and supplies and fans of one airflow only go in. The supply and fan bays are shown open.

dc-f2b.description: QFX5220-128C-D-AFO: four 1600 W DC supplies (JPSU-1600W-DC-AFO) and six front-to-back fan modules. The DC supplies take a D-Sub 3W3 connector (guide, QFX5220-128C DC Power Cable Specification).

description: Juniper QFX5220-128C, a 4RU 100G data-centre spine switch that runs Junos OS Evolved. It has 128 QSFP28 ports (100 or 40 GbE, 32 of them channelizable to 4 x 25 GbE) and two SFP+ ports (10 GbE only). The QSFP28 ports stand in four rows of 32, as stacked pairs, and each port has four lamps. The port side also carries an RJ-45 time-of-day port and four clock connectors (PPS and 10 MHz, in and out). It has an RJ-45 console port, an RJ-45 management port, a USB port, the reset button, three chassis lamps and the ESD point. The rear carries four power supplies and six two-fan modules. It ships in AC and DC builds with front-to-back (AIR OUT) airflow only. A spare chassis has no supplies and no fan modules.

gaps.wanted: Packet rate, buffer size and latency. The guide states none of them. They are in the QFX5220 datasheet, and Juniper's addresses for it redirect to an hpe.com PSNow page that did not answer when tried, so the datasheet was not read.
The depth of the fan module. The guide's figures are photographs and drawings with no scale, and its tables state weights only for the whole chassis.
Whether the console and management RJ-45 jacks have lamps. The drawing shows none, and the guide describes lamps for the 32CD's management port only (Table 15). They are not drawn.
Whether the time-of-day RJ-45 jack has lamps. The drawing shows none, and the guide describes none.

The connector type of the four clock jacks. Figure 17's callout 3 says "SMB In, SMB Out, 10 MHz In, 10 MHz Out". Figure 21's callout 3 says "PPS Out, PPS In, 10 MHz Out, 10 MHz In". The jacks are 6.9 mm across in the drawing, which is SMA size and not SMB size. They are drawn as the library's SMA jack. Estimated.
The USB revision. Figure 17 says "USB 2.0 port". The port is drawn with the kit's neutral usb2 skin.

The speeds of the two SFP+ ports. The 128C description says "10 Gigabit or 1 Gigabit Ethernet support" and figure 21 says "1-Gbps or 10-Gbps ports". The Network Ports note says "The last two SFP+ ports cannot support 1GbE modules". The ports are modelled at 10g, the one speed all three agree on.

Which of the four small arrow windows in the SFP+ light pipe is which lamp. Table 10 gives each port a link and activity lamp and a status lamp. The windows are assigned from the arrows and the assignment is estimated.
Which row of windows in a cell's light pipe serves which port. Table 9 gives each port up to four lamps. The upper row is assigned to the upper port from the arrows and the assignment is estimated.

A library part for the two tapped holes of the protective earthing terminal. The pair parts in the library compose screw heads, and the guide says the screws are not supplied. The plate and the earth symbol are drawn and the two holes are not.

The guide's QFX5220-128C Port Panel topic holds a section headed QFX5230-64CD Port Panel (a 64 QSFP56-DD port panel, with the sentence "2xSFP+ user ports" and "2x DIN connectors" for the clock). It does not describe the 128C, and nothing in it is used. The QFX5230-64CD is not modelled here.
The width and depth. Guide Table 32 says 17.32 in and 29.25 in. Juniper's Hardware Compatibility Tool says 17.26 in and 29 in. The guide's table is used.
The rack ears' positions and the rack kit's contract. The guide names QFX5220-4PRMK-4U and gives two different rail spacings. No kit contract exists in the library and none is written here.

esd.description: the wrist-strap ESD point on the port side (guide figure 21, callout 9)

fan-leds.description: The round status lamp beside each fan module - green when the module is healthy, amber blinking on an error (guide Table 17).

attrs.redundancy-note: QFX5220 hardware guide, QFX5220 Component Redundancy: the QFX5220-128C has 12 fans in 6 fan modules, one fan of the 12 for redundancy, (5x2+1)+1; any further failure causes overheating, alarms and a shutdown

mgmt.mixed: the out-of-band cluster at the right of the port side - an RJ-45 console port, an RJ-45 management port, a USB port and the recessed reset button. Four kinds, one purpose: reaching and recovering the switch when the data plane cannot.

attrs.redundancy-note: four supplies, two of which carry the whole switch; a pair of two works only as supplies (0,2), (0,3), (1,2) or (1,3)

qsfp28-0-31.description: The first cell row of the upper block, ports 0 to 31, the even port above the odd in each cell, and the ports of one cell a pair.

qsfp28-32-63.description: The second cell row of the upper block, ports 32 to 63.

qsfp28-64-95.description: The first cell row of the lower block, ports 64 to 95.

qsfp28-96-127.description: The second cell row of the lower block, ports 96 to 127.

qsfp28-leds.description: Four lamps per QSFP28 port, one per channel, in the light pipe of its cell. The leftmost shows the link of a port that is not channelized (guide Table 9).

sfp-plus.description: Ports 128 and 129 as printed, rel-pos carrying the printed number, since the origin token cannot express a block that starts at 128.

sfp-plus-leds.description: Two lamps per SFP+ port - link and activity at the left, status at the right (guide Table 10).

status-leds.description: The three chassis lamps ALM, SYS and ID (guide Table 14).

timing.mixed: the time and frequency block at the right of the port side - an RJ-45 time-of-day port and four clock connectors (PPS and 10 MHz, in and out). Five jacks of two kinds, one purpose: moving a timing reference into or out of the switch.

name: qfx5220-128c

chassis.note: guide Table 32: 6.88 in (17.48 cm) high, 17.32 in (44 cm) wide, 29.25 in (74.3 cm) deep, 98 lb (44.45 kg) with power supplies and fans installed and 76 lb (34.47 kg) chassis only. The inch figures are used and the centimetre ones in the same cell are rounded copies. 6.88 in is 4RU less the usual clearance (4 x 44.45 = 177.8 mm), so ru is 4. Juniper's Hardware Compatibility Tool says 6.88 x 17.26 x 29 in (17.48 x 43.84 x 73.66 cm) and 98 lb. Width and depth disagree between the two. The guide's table is used. The width is the body: the outer edges of the front mounting flanges extend it to 19 in, so the flanges are not part of the body and are not modelled.

clock-connectors.note: Figure 17 callout 3: four coaxial jacks 6.9 mm across in two columns and two rows, at 402.5 and 413.1 mm across and 54.9 and 63.0 mm down (centres). The left column prints PPS and the right 10M, the upper row OUT and the lower IN. Callout 3's list in figure 17 reads "SMB In, SMB Out, 10 MHz In, 10 MHz Out" and figure 21's list reads "PPS Out, PPS In, 10 MHz Out, 10 MHz In".

colour.note: The front plate is the grey of the 32CD's (#8a8a8b), which figure 12 matches by eye. No sample was taken from the 128C photograph, which is small and lit warmly. It is estimated.

drawing-vs-photo.note: Figure 13 (photograph) and figure 32 (drawing) agree on the rear. Figure 12 (photograph) and figure 17 (drawing) agree on the front, with two differences. The photograph shows no lamp windows on the RJ-45 jacks, as the drawing does. The photograph shows the model name at a larger size than the 32CD's. The photograph's SFP+ and RJ-45 shields are the same as the drawing's. The photograph of the real device is followed where it shows more.

ears-and-kits.note: NOT MODELLED, provenance only. The guide names the rack mount kit QFX5220-4PRMK-4U (mounting rails, rear mounting blades, a flange and screws, shipped in the box) for a four-post rack, and says the front and rear rack rails must be 28 in (71.1 cm) to 36 in (91.4 cm) apart. The guide's site section says 23.6 to 36 in. The two ranges disagree. No kit contract is written here and `chassis.ears` and `chassis.kits` are left out. The modelled body is the 439.9 mm chassis, without flanges.

earthing-terminal.note: The chassis protective earthing terminal (callout 3 of figure 32) at the lower left of the rear: a plate 27.5 mm by 9.7 mm at 14.6 mm and 147.5 mm down with two tapped holes 15.9 mm apart (the guide's Panduit LCD10-10A-L lug, 5/8 in centres, takes two 10-32 screws that the box does not include) and the earth symbol at 49.5 mm. The plate and the symbol are drawn. The two holes are not, because the library has no part for a bare pair of tapped holes (see gaps).

gate-1.note: Figure 17 (g051150) is a flat line drawing. Its body is 1413.5 px wide and 563 px high, an aspect of 2.511 against the table's 439.9 / 174.8 = 2.517 (0.2 percent out), so it carries geometry. Scale 3.213 px/mm across and 3.222 px/mm down, origin at the left and top edges of the body. Figure 32 (g051151, the rear) is 1415 by 565 px, aspect 2.504 (0.5 percent out), 3.217 px/mm across and 3.233 down. Every position below is read off these two at 4 to 6 times zoom and is estimated to about 0.3 mm. The photographs (figures 12 and 13, 2.66 px/mm) agree with the drawings to 0.7 mm across and 2 mm down. The photograph is foreshortened a little, and the drawings are used for every position.

lifecycle.note: Searched for an end-of-life announcement. No Juniper notice was found and the guide, published 2026-10-14, states none. The third-party trackers searched list nothing for the QFX5220. The device states none announced. Estimated, because the trackers are not the maker.

light-pipe.note: The light pipe is the pale strip between the ports of a cell, 6.3 mm high, and the pipe of the two cells of a housing is drawn as one strip. The colour is read from the photograph and is estimated. The pipe carries a small outlined up-arrow at 2.1 mm and a down-arrow at 16.3 mm from the cell's left edge. They are moulded into the pipe, they sit under the lamp windows of the cell, and they are not drawn: a mark drawn there would stand inside the lamp bezels.

logo.note: The maker's logo and its lockup are printed at the upper right of the face, 380.6 to 412.4 mm across and 20.0 to 28.4 mm down, above the model name QFX5220-128C. The logo is not drawn: a logo-zone region is reserved where it stands, and the model name is drawn as plain text.

mgmt-panel.note: Figure 17 and figure 21: below the clock connectors, from the left, a stacked pair of RJ-45 jacks in one shield 17.9 mm wide at 395.9 mm (the upper jack the console, callout 6, and the lower the management port, callout 10, as the legend "CON up-arrow, down-arrow MGMT" below them says), a USB-A port standing on its side 6.0 mm wide and 13.4 mm high (callout 7), the RESET pinhole (callout 8) and the ESD point with its warning mark (callout 9). The ESD point is at 416.9 mm and 145.0 mm down and its warning mark 3.5 mm to its left. The mark is drawn 2.6 mm further left, to clear the 6.0 mm bezel of the library's ESD jack. The jacks have no lamps in figure 17 and the guide describes no lamps for the 128C's management port. The USB mark is printed above the port. The three chassis lamps ALM, SYS and ID (callout 4) stand in a column at 420.3 mm, 56.3, 62.3 and 68.3 mm down, each with its legend above it. The serial number slide-out tab (callout 11) is at the bottom, left of the centre.

modules.note: The six fan modules (QFX5220-128C-FANAO, Table 3) and the four power supplies (JPSU-1600W-AC-AFO and JPSU-1600W-DC-AFO, Tables 3, 18 and 25) are field-replaceable units in bays, each its own component. The supplies carry the same part numbers as the QFX10002's supplies, and the QFX10002 components for them exist, so they are reused as they are. The fan module is new. Each supply carries two small counter-rotating fans inside. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit that is not a bay. The status lamp of each fan is on the chassis strip beside its module (figure 27).

port-lamps.note: Table 9 gives each QSFP28 port one lamp per channel, and the leftmost lamp shows the link of a port that is not channelized. Figure 18 callout 1 and figure 17 show eight small windows in the light pipe of each cell, in two rows of four, between an up-arrow at the left and a down-arrow at the right. The upper row is read as the four lamps of the upper port and the lower row as those of the lower port, because the arrows point at the ports. That assignment is estimated: no table says which row is which. A window is 2.2 mm wide and 1.45 mm high on a 2.55 mm pitch and the two rows are 1.55 mm apart. The four windows of one port are one component of this family, juniper/qfx5220-128c-port-lamps, because the library's small bar lamp is 2.8 by 1.6 mm and overlaps its neighbours on this pitch. The first window of a port starts 4.4 mm right of the cell's left edge, and the rows are 11.13 mm and 12.68 mm below the top of the cell housing. The lamps are unlit in the photograph. No hole is punched for them, since the windows are filled by the light pipe.

port-numbering.note: Printed on the metal and read off figure 17 at 6 times zoom. Over the first cell row, the even numbers 0 to 30. Under it, in the gap between the rows, "n up-arrow, down-arrow m": the odd numbers 1 to 31 and the even numbers 32 to 62, the odd one for the lower port of the cell above and the even one for the upper port of the cell below. Under the second row, the odd numbers 33 to 63. The lower block repeats this from 64: 64 to 94 above, "65 up-arrow, down-arrow 96" in the gap, 97 to 127 under. So the ports of cell row 1 are 0 to 31, of row 2 32 to 63, of row 3 64 to 95 and of row 4 96 to 127. The odd number is the lower port of a cell in every row. The two SFP+ ports print 128 above and 129 below. The guide numbers the network ports 0 to 127 and the SFP+ ports 128 and 129 (the QSFP28 network port text and callout 5). Interface names are not printed. The guide's examples name them et-0/0/N on one FPC and PIC, always 0, so port N is et-0/0/N and the SFP+ pair is et-0/0/128 and et-0/0/129; that is recorded here and not in an interfaces block, because the face does not print it.

ports.note: Figure 17: 128 QSFP28 ports in two blocks of four rows. Each cell is a stacked pair, an upper and a lower port with a light pipe between them, and 16 cells make a row of the block, in eight pairs of cells. A cell opening is 18.5 mm wide, the registry's QSFP ganged cell, on a 19.0 mm pitch. The pairs are 44.9 mm apart, so the gutter is 6.9 mm. The first opening starts at 19.1 mm (the housing outline at 18.6 mm). The housings measure 38.9 mm across a pair and 25.6 mm high. The tops of the housings lie at 21.7 and 51.8 mm down in the upper block and at 104.5 and 134.5 mm in the lower block. The two ports of a cell are 15.9 mm apart, the housing's 25.6 less one opening, the 9.58 mm opening of the registry. The vertical readings come off the drawing and the figure 13 photograph agrees to 2 mm, the photograph being foreshortened. The two SFP+ ports stand at the right of the lower block, stacked, callout 5.

power.note: Table 19 (AC): 100 to 240 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz, 19.36 A at 100 to 127 VAC and 10.95 A at 200 to 240 VAC, typical 942 W and maximum 1506 W at 220 to 240 V. Table 26 (DC): rated -48 to -60 VDC, range -40 to -72 VDC, 40 A maximum, typical 955 W and maximum 1530 W. The guide's note: maximum measured at 40 C ambient with SR optics at 100 percent load with IMIX traffic; typical at 25 C with DACs at 50 percent load with IMIX traffic. The AC pair is the device's, since AC is the default build, and the DC pair is carried under its own keys. Four supplies give 2+2 redundancy (the guide's component redundancy section), and a pair of two is valid only as (0,2), (0,3), (1,2) or (1,3).

rear-layout.note: Figure 32 (g051151) at 3.217 px/mm across and 3.233 down. Six fan modules in two rows of three, each 80.0 mm by 81.5 mm on a 90.0 mm pitch across (the first at 90.2 mm) and an 85.4 mm pitch down (the top row at 6.5 mm and the lower at 91.9 mm). Four supply bays, one in each corner of the face: 74.1 mm by 40.6 mm at 4.4 mm and 363.4 mm across and 11.4 mm and 94.4 mm down. The numbers printed on the plates read 0 (upper left), 1 (upper right), 2 (lower left) and 3 (lower right). That agrees with the guide's rule that two supplies are valid as (0,2), (0,3), (1,2) or (1,3) and not as (0,1) or (2,3), the pairs on one row. Each fan has a fan symbol, its number and a round lamp window on the strip at its right: 175.4 mm, 265.4 mm and 355.4 mm across, the lamp 75.6 mm down on the top row and 160.9 mm on the lower. The fan modules are numbered "from top left 0 to bottom right 5". The supply bay size is the QFX10002 supply's (the part with the same part number), which agrees with the drawing to 0.4 mm.

serial-tab.note: A flat tab 16.5 mm wide and 3.3 mm high at 383.1 mm and 163.4 mm down, callout 11 of figure 17, the chassis serial number slide-out tab. It is light blue in the photograph. It is drawn as decor, because it is a label card and not a part the library models.

sfp-plus.note: Figure 17 and figure 18 callout 2: a stacked pair, the housing 15.7 mm wide at 377.7 mm and 25.9 mm high from 104.1 mm, with a light pipe between the cages carrying four small arrow windows. Table 10 gives each SFP+ port two lamps, link and activity at the left and status at the right. The four windows are drawn as four lamps in the pipe, the left pair the link lamps and the right pair the status lamps. Which port each window serves is estimated, from the arrows (down-arrow for the lower port, up-arrow for the upper). The lower cage is turned 180 degrees as in the QFX5130-32CD.

sources.note: Juniper QFX5220 Switch Hardware Guide, published 2026-10-14, 321 pages (copyright Hewlett Packard Enterprise), from juniper.net. Used here: the front and FRU panel figures 12 and 13 (photographs of the real unit, 1500 x 543 px in the PDF, g100562 and g100563), the flat drawings figure 17 (g051150, the port panel and its callouts), figure 18 (g051178, the lamps), figure 21 (the management panel) and figure 32 (g051151, the flat FRU panel), Tables 3 and 8 to 10 (components and lamps), Tables 14 and 17 (chassis and fan lamps), Table 16, the cooling and power sections (Tables 18, 19, 25 to 29 and figures 25 to 27, 35, 38), Table 31 (environment) and Table 32 (physical specifications). The QFX5220 datasheet could not be read: the maker's addresses for it redirect to an hpe.com PSNow page that did not answer when tried, so no datasheet is registered. The part numbers of the orderable variants come from Juniper's Hardware Compatibility Tool page for the QFX5220-128C (apps.juniper.net/hct), the maker's own tool. No studio photograph was found on juniper.net, and no Visio stencil or 3D model was found. The guide's flat drawings are the measured sources and its photographs are the checks. The guide and the tool are the maker's and public. The guide is copyrighted and nothing in it is copied.

stack-orientation.note: Figure 17 draws the latch tab at the top of both ports of a cell, so neither is turned. This differs from the QSFP-DD stack of the 32CD and from the library's convention for stacked cages, and it is read from a drawing, so it is estimated.

tod-jack.note: Callout 2, "RJ-45 grandmaster time-of-day connection", printed ToD: a jack in a shield 17.4 mm wide and 13.9 mm high at 377.9 mm and 51.6 mm down, with the latch slot at the bottom (the library's housing as it comes). It has no lamps in the drawing.

variants.note: Juniper's Hardware Compatibility Tool lists QFX5220-128C-AFO (AC) and QFX5220-128C-D-AFO (DC), both front-to-back, and guide Table 3 names the spare chassis QFX5220-128C-CHAS. Table 3 says the 128C is not available with back-to-front airflow. All three share this front panel and the rear bays, so each is a configuration of this device. NOT MODELLED: the EMI front panel (QFX5220-141-EMI-DR, a spare order number the guide gives in Table 46), a cover for the port side.

vents.note: Hexagonal holes in the sheet: a band above the first row (5.1 to 17.2 mm down), a band between the two blocks (80.7 to 100.2 mm), a band along the bottom (164 to 172.6 mm), a field at each end of the face, and a column of seven round holes in each gutter between pairs of cells, for each row. The photograph (figure 12) shows the hexagonal holes 6.6 mm apart along a row. The tile is set to a 6.5 mm pitch. The gutter holes are 7 a row on a 3.76 mm pitch read at figure 17's scale. All of it is drawn as vent decor and is estimated.

stack-exceptions.reason: Read from the guide's flat drawing, figure 17 (g051150), at 6 times zoom: both ports of every cell draw their latch tab at the top of the opening, and a stacked cell with a light pipe between its ports is one moulding, so both ports are the same way up. The 128C's photograph (figure 12) shows the same tabs at its own small scale. No close photograph of a cell is held, so the reading comes from a drawing and is estimated; see provenance.stack-orientation.

bottom.empty: Not drawn by any source held. The guide's figures show no underside, and the photographs and drawings are of the front and rear only.

placements.description: Table 14 - red steady: major hardware fault; amber steady: minor system alarm; unlit: no alarm or halted
Table 14 - green steady: Junos OS Evolved is loaded; unlit: powered off or halted
Table 14 - blue blinking: the beacon feature is enabled (request chassis beacon fpc 0 on); unlit: not enabled

left.empty: Not drawn by any source held. The mounting figures show the rails on a side wall in perspective only, with no scale from which a hole could be placed.

right.empty: Not drawn by any source held. No figure shows the right wall flat.

top.empty: Not drawn by any source held. The guide gives no figure of the lid, and the photographs and drawings are straight-on of the front and rear only.
